scan.coverageLimitation: This engine evaluates what the providers below publish. There is no global cell-by-cell scan, and no claim is made about hazards outside each provider’s stated reach. A place absent from every provider was not examined and must not be read as quiet.

providers.label: GDACS (Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System)
providers.inputBasis: GDACS raises alerts on events it has already detected, so its records say what is happening rather than what will.
providers.coverageResolution: Only events GDACS itself raises to an alert level. Flood, drought and wildfire records describe alert areas, not incident points.
providers.completenessBasis: GDACS lists only events it raises to an alert level, so a disaster it does not carry may simply be below that threshold.

providers.label: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
providers.inputBasis: A catalogue of earthquakes that have occurred.
providers.coverageResolution: Every earthquake of magnitude 2.5 or above in the past seven days, at its epicentre. Anything smaller, or older, is outside this feed.
providers.completenessBasis: A complete catalogue of earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 and above for the past seven days, so an absence above that threshold is meaningful.

providers.label: EMSC (European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre)
providers.inputBasis: A catalogue of earthquakes that have occurred.
providers.geographicCoverage: Global, with the densest network in Europe and the Mediterranean
providers.coverageResolution: Earthquakes of magnitude 4.5 or above, at epicentre.

providers.label: NASA EONET
providers.inputBasis: A curated catalogue of natural events already under way.
providers.coverageResolution: A curated set of events drawn from Earth-observation sources. EONET does not claim to list every event, so absence here is not evidence of absence.
providers.completenessBasis: A curated set; EONET does not claim to list every event, so its silence is not evidence.

providers.label: NOAA National Hurricane Center
providers.inputBasis: The hurricane centre publishes advisories for active systems, including where a storm is expected to go, which is an input to a forecast of what it has not yet done.
providers.geographicCoverage: Atlantic, eastern Pacific and central Pacific basins only
providers.coverageResolution: Active tropical cyclones, at storm centre. Storms in the western Pacific, Indian Ocean and southern hemisphere are outside this provider entirely.
providers.completenessBasis: Every active tropical cyclone in the basins it publishes for.

providers.label: NOAA / National Weather Service
providers.inputBasis: A watch or warning states that severe weather is expected, which is a statement about what has not happened yet.
providers.geographicCoverage: United States and its territories only
providers.coverageResolution: Alerts at severe or extreme severity, carrying the affected-area polygon where the agency published one and a forecast-zone centre where it did not.
providers.completenessBasis: Exhaustive for active warnings, but a warning is not an observation: these records never enter the observed-disaster ledger, so this provider cannot establish that no disaster occurred.
providers.failureReason: 1 alert(s) could not be placed and were left out.

providers.label: ReliefWeb (UN OCHA)
providers.inputBasis: Situation reports and declarations published after a disaster has occurred.
providers.coverageResolution: Country-level humanitarian disaster declarations. These carry no incident coordinates and are placed at a country centroid.
providers.completenessBasis: Only disasters ReliefWeb has declared, which is a subset of those that occur.
providers.failureReason: 1 declaration(s) named a country that could not be resolved and were left out.

providers.label: USGS Volcano Hazards Program
providers.inputBasis: A volcano alert level states expected activity - a watch or warning is issued for unrest before an eruption, not after it.
providers.geographicCoverage: Volcanoes monitored by the United States volcano observatories
providers.coverageResolution: Volcanoes currently at an elevated alert level. Volcanoes outside the US observatory network are not covered by this provider.
providers.completenessBasis: Exhaustive for elevated alert levels in the observatory network it covers, which is not the same as exhaustive for eruptions that caused harm: an alert level is a published status, these records never enter the observed-disaster ledger, and their silence establishes only that nothing was elevated.
